{{Short description|English mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Percy John Harding''' (15 June 1845, London – 1943?) was an English mathematician, noteworthy as an [[invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1912.<ref>{{cite book|chapter=The geometry of Thales|author=Harding, P. J.|volume=2|pages=533–538|title=Proceedings of the Fifth International Congress of Mathematicians (Cambridge, 22–28 August 1912)|chapter-url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=njp.32101039891054;view=1up;seq=539}}</ref>

The elder son of William Harding, a surgeon in London, Percy J. Harding received his B.A. in 1869 and his M.A. in 1874 from [[Cambridge University]]. He became a lecturer at [[University College, London]] and [[Bedford College, London]].<ref>{{acad|id=HRDN865PJ|name=Harding, Percy John}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=The Journal of Education|year=1893|page=184|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qihKAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA184}}</ref> On 1 March 1906 at Bedford College, London, he gave a talk ''The History and Human Side of Mathematics'' with lantern illustrations.<ref>{{cite book|title=The Education Outlook, volumes 59 & 60|year=1906|page=131|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dNcgAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA131}}</ref> Using lantern slides, he gave a talk ''The history and evolution of arithmetic division'' at the ICM at 9 PM on 22 August 1912 in Cambridge, England.<ref>{{cite book|editor=Hobson, E. B.|editor2=Love, A. E. H.|title=Proceedings of the Fifth International Congress of Mathematicians|publisher=University Press|year=1913|page=[https://archive.org/details/proceedingsfifth00hobs_333/page/n45 46]|url=https://archive.org/details/proceedingsfifth00hobs_333}}</ref>
